candidates.label: The doubtless Book as guidance
candidates.definition: The opening declaration that the Book is free from doubt and serves as guidance.

evidence.excerpt: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَۛ فِيهِۛ هُدٗى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ
evidence.rationale: Verse explicitly describes the Book as doubtless guidance.

candidates.arabicLabel: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَۛ فِيهِۛ هُدٗى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ

candidates.label: Taqwa as condition for receiving guidance
candidates.definition: Taqwa identified in 2:2 as the condition for benefiting from the Book's guidance.

evidence.excerpt: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَۛ فِيهِۛ هُدٗى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ
evidence.rationale: Guidance explicitly specified for the muttaqin.

candidates.label: Belief in the unseen (iman bil-ghayb)
candidates.definition: Faith in al-ghayb listed as first quality of muttaqin in 2:3.

evidence.excerpt: ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
evidence.rationale: Belief in the unseen explicitly named.

candidates.label: Establishing prayer (iqamat as-salah)
candidates.definition: Establishment of salah as second quality of muttaqin in 2:3.

evidence.excerpt: ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
evidence.rationale: Establishing prayer explicitly named.

candidates.label: Spending from divine provision (infaq mimma razaqna)
candidates.definition: Spending from what Allah provided, third quality of muttaqin in 2:3.

evidence.excerpt: ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
evidence.rationale: Spending from divine provision explicitly named.

candidates.label: Certainty in the Hereafter (yaqin bil-akhirah)
candidates.definition: Absolute certainty regarding the Hereafter in 2:4.

evidence.excerpt: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبۡلِكَ وَبِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ يُوقِنُونَ
evidence.rationale: Certainty in Hereafter explicitly stated.

candidates.label: Success (falah) as outcome of divine guidance
candidates.definition: State of being muflihun declared in 2:5 for those upon guidance.

evidence.excerpt: أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدٗى مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ وَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
evidence.rationale: Success explicitly declared.

candidates.notes: Gap candidate: no existing topic addresses falah specifically.

candidates.label: Disbelief (kufr) and ineffectiveness of warning
candidates.definition: State in 2:6 where disbelief renders warning equivalent to non-warning.

evidence.excerpt: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
evidence.rationale: Complete verse states equivalence.

candidates.urduLabel: کفر اور انذار کی بے اثری

candidates.label: Sealing of hearts, hearing, and veiling of sight
candidates.definition: Divine act in 2:7 of sealing hearts/hearing and veiling sight. Theology deferred.

evidence.excerpt: خَتَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ وَعَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِمۡۖ وَعَلَىٰٓ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ غِشَٰوَةٞۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٞ
evidence.rationale: Complete verse describes seal, veil, and punishment.

candidates.urduLabel: قلوب پر مہر اور بصارت پر پردہ
candidates.notes: Gap candidate. Most theologically significant verse in opening of Al-Baqarah.

candidates.label: False profession of faith without possessing it
candidates.definition: Phenomenon in 2:8 of verbal profession without actual belief.

evidence.excerpt: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَمَا هُم بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
evidence.rationale: Verse contrasts verbal profession with actual belief.

candidates.label: Self-deception (attempting to deceive Allah but deceiving only oneself)

evidence.excerpt: يُخَٰدِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَمَا يَخۡدَعُونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَمَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
evidence.rationale: Verse states they deceive only themselves.

candidates.label: Disease in the heart (marad fil-qulub) and its increase
candidates.definition: Spiritual disease in hearts described in 2:10, increased by Allah.

evidence.excerpt: فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٞ فَزَادَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَرَضٗاۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمُۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡذِبُونَ
evidence.rationale: Verse names disease, increase, and links punishment to lying.

candidates.urduLabel: قلوب کا مرض اور اس میں اضافہ
candidates.notes: Nature of marad and theology of increase deferred to tafsir.

candidates.label: Corruption on earth (fasad fil-ard) and its denial
candidates.definition: Prohibition against corruption (2:11) and false claim of being reformers.

evidence.excerpt: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ لَا تُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا نَحۡنُ مُصۡلِحُونَ
evidence.rationale: Command and false response both explicit.

evidence.excerpt: أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدُونَ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَشۡعُرُونَ
evidence.rationale: Divine correction: they are the corrupters.

candidates.urduLabel: فساد فی الارض اور مصلحین کا دعویی

candidates.label: Arrogance toward believers — calling them foolish
candidates.definition: Arrogance in 2:13 calling believers foolish; divine reversal.

evidence.excerpt: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ ءَامِنُواْ كَمَآ ءَامَنَ ٱلنَّاسُ قَالُوٓاْ أَنُؤۡمِنُ كَمَآ ءَامَنَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُۗ أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَعۡلَمُونَ
evidence.rationale: Verse contains arrogant claim and divine reversal.

candidates.label: Double-faced conduct — public profession vs. private alliance
candidates.definition: Dual behavior in 2:14: professing belief publicly, declaring alliance with shayatin privately.

evidence.excerpt: وَإِذَا لَقُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ شَيَٰطِينِهِمۡ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا مَعَكُمۡ إِنَّمَا نَحۡنُ مُسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
evidence.rationale: Both faces explicitly stated in single verse.

existingTopicOverlap.note: Word nifaq not in text; description matches.

candidates.label: Trading guidance for misguidance — the profitless transaction
candidates.definition: Commercial metaphor in 2:16 for spiritual exchange.

evidence.excerpt: أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشۡتَرَوُاْ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ فَمَا رَبِحَت تِّجَٰرَتُهُمۡ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُهۡتَدِينَ
evidence.rationale: Commercial metaphor explicit throughout verse.

candidates.urduLabel: ہدایت کے بدلے گمراہی کی تجارت
candidates.notes: Gap candidate: Quranic commercial metaphor for spiritual choices.

candidates.label: Parable of the kindled fire — light given then withdrawn
candidates.definition: First parable in 2:17 comparing hypocrites to one whose fire-light was taken away.

evidence.excerpt: مَثَلُهُمۡ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِي ٱسۡتَوۡقَدَ نَارٗا فَلَمَّآ أَضَآءَتۡ مَا حَوۡلَهُۥ ذَهَبَ ٱللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمۡ وَتَرَكَهُمۡ فِي ظُلُمَٰتٖ لَّا يُبۡصِرُونَ
evidence.rationale: Parable explicitly introduced with mathaluhum kamathali.

candidates.notes: Gap candidate: Quranic parables (amthal) not represented in taxonomy.

candidates.label: Parable of the rainstorm — darkness, thunder, lightning, fear of death
candidates.definition: Second parable in 2:19-20: rainstorm with darkness, thunder, lightning.

evidence.excerpt: أَوۡ كَصَيِّبٖ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَٰتٞ وَرَعۡدٞ وَبَرۡقٞ يَجۡعَلُونَ أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ فِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۚ وَٱللَّهُ مُحِيطُۢ بِٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
evidence.rationale: Rainstorm parable begins with aw kasayyibin.

evidence.excerpt: يَكَادُ ٱلۡبَرۡقُ يَخۡطَفُ أَبۡصَٰرَهُمۡۖ كُلَّمَآ أَضَآءَ لَهُم مَّشَوۡاْ فِيهِ وَإِذَآ أَظۡلَمَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ قَامُواْۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمۡعِهِمۡ وَأَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٞ
evidence.rationale: Continuation with lightning/sight imagery and divine power.
